final_answer: D-glucuronic acid and N-acetyl-D-glucosamine, joined by alternating beta(1->4) and beta(1->3) glycosidic bonds.
note: Evidence PMC6245326 states the disaccharide sugars are D-glucuronic acid and D-N-acetylglucosamine linked through alternating beta-1,4 and beta-1,3 glycosidic bonds; PMC4542320 gives the same [beta1,4-GlcUA-beta-1,3-GlcNAc-]n structure.

final_answer: At the plasma membrane by hyaluronan synthases (HAS1/2/3), which extrude the growing chain directly into the extracellular space. Other GAGs are built in the Golgi on a core protein; HA has no core protein.
note: Evidence PMC4039572 states HA does not require a core protein, is not synthesized in the Golgi, and is produced at the plasma membrane by HAS1, 2, 3; PMC4401461 states the chain is extruded directly into the extracellular space.

final_answer: It is non-sulfated, and it is not covalently attached to a core protein.
note: Evidence supports non-sulfated HA only indirectly (PMC5093463 contrasts sulfated HA with 'non-sulfated HA'), and no window states that HA itself is not covalently attached to a core protein; the core-protein windows concern chondroitin sulfate/UTI, so the second feature is not settled.

final_answer: Hyaluronidases (HYAL1, HYAL2, and PH-20/SPAM1), with additional catabolic routes via CEMIP (KIAA1199) and TMEM2; reactive oxygen species also fragment HA non-enzymatically.
note: Evidence PMC13506898 lists the HA catabolic enzymes as HYAL1, HYAL2 and SPAM1 (PH-20), HYBID (also known as CEMIP or KIAA1199), and TMEM2.

final_answer: It is embryonic lethal, with severe cardiac and vascular defects (failure of endocardial cushion formation), showing HA is essential for development.
note: Evidence PMC3795687 states Has2 KO mice show severe cardiac defects from abnormal cardiac cushion mesenchyme formation and early lethality at the cushion-formation stage; PMC4044312 states has2 disruption abrogates AVC endocardial cushion formation.

final_answer: Karl Meyer (1934), from bovine vitreous humor; the name combines 'hyalos' (Greek for glass, describing the vitreous) with 'uronic acid'.
note: No evidence window mentions Karl Meyer, 1934, isolation from bovine vitreous, or the hyalos/uronic-acid naming; the windows discuss vitreous mechanics and substitutes only, so none of the draft's claims are settled.

final_answer: UDP-glucuronic acid and UDP-N-acetylglucosamine, added alternately to the growing chain.
note: Evidence PMC4039572 states HAS use cytosolic UDP-GlcUA and UDP-GlcNAc substrates; PMC13061412 states synthesis involves alternately binding UDP-GlcA and UDP-GlcNAc.

final_answer: Very long chains entangle into a transient network and bind large amounts of water; under shear the chains align and disentangle, so viscosity falls (shear-thinning) and recovers at rest.
note: Evidence confirms shear-thinning/viscoelastic behavior and water-binding and mentions 'structural reorganization within the polymer network' under shear (PMC12733943), but no window supports the draft's mechanism of chain entanglement, alignment/disentanglement under shear, or recovery at rest.

final_answer: HA can bind 10 to 10,000 times more water than its own weight.
note: Evidence PMC12114106 states HA is 'able to bind 10 to 10,000 times more water than its weight', so the draft's 'up to about 1,000 times' understates the evidenced range.

final_answer: Streptococcus zooepidemicus (group C streptococci) for fermentation; rooster combs for animal extraction.
note: Evidence PMC5727345 states commercial HA comes from extraction from rooster comb and fermentation of group A and C Streptococcus; PMC6482233 identifies S. zooepidemicus as the significant industrial streptococcal species and PMC9966800 discusses its fermentation.

final_answer: C - plasma membrane, by HAS enzymes that extrude the chain directly outside the cell.
note: Evidence PMC4581547 states hyaluronan is synthesized at the plasma membrane by HAS1, 2 and 3 and extruded directly into extracellular space, matching option C.

final_answer: HAS adds new sugars to the REDUCING end of the growing chain (the chain is extruded through the membrane as it grows) - the opposite of most polysaccharide synthesis, which elongates the non-reducing end.
note: Evidence is contradictory: PMC4401461 states HAS 'adds them alternately to the reducing end of the chain', while PMC4834982 states HA synthases transfer sugars 'to the nonreducing end of a growing HA chain'; the pack does not resolve which is correct.

final_answer: The umbilical cord - its Wharton's jelly is an HA-rich mucoid connective tissue (an early commercial HA source).
note: Evidence PMC12903654 describes Wharton's jelly as the mucoid connective tissue surrounding umbilical cord vessels whose matrix includes hyaluronic acid; PMC7659052 states Wharton's jelly in the umbilical cord is largely composed of hyaluronic acid.

final_answer: About half (~7-8 g of the ~15 g total in a 70 kg adult).
note: No evidence window gives the fraction of body HA in skin or any total-body HA amount (e.g. ~15 g / ~7-8 g); the windows concern collagen peptides, skin elasticity measurements and skin-type classification only.

final_answer: HAS1 and HAS2 produce longer HA chains than HAS3 (Has1 = Has2 > Has3); HAS3 produces lower-mass HA (e.g., <200,000 Da), and HAS2 is the most active and highly expressed of the three isoforms.
note: Evidence PMC3360468 states 'the average polymer length of HA synthesized by each type of Has enzyme is different (Has1 = Has2 > Has3)' with lower-mass HA '(<200,000 Da), such as that produced by Has3', and PMC4758074 states 'HAS2 is the most active and highly expressed' - contradicting the draft's HAS2-only longest chains, its grouped 0.2-2 MDa range, and HAS3 being most active.

final_answer: It colorimetrically measures uronic acid content after acid hydrolysis; since every HA disaccharide carries one glucuronic acid, it serves as a classic (if not fully specific) HA quantification assay.
note: The only on-point evidence (PMC4445729) merely names the 'uronic acid carbazole assay' as a less sensitive GAG assay; no window establishes the colorimetric acid-hydrolysis procedure or that one glucuronic acid per HA disaccharide makes it an HA quantification assay.

final_answer: They use HA-binding protein (HABP, e.g., from bovine cartilage) in a sandwich/competitive format - HABP binds HA with high specificity, replacing antibodies that HA (a non-immunogenic molecule) cannot raise.
note: Evidence is almost entirely off-topic; the only relevant fragment is a section title on preparation of biotinylated hyaluronan binding protein from bovine nasal septum cartilage (PMC4234048). No window describes a sandwich/competitive HABP assay format, HABP specificity replacing antibodies, or HA being non-immunogenic.

final_answer: The HA-rich pericellular coat (glycocalyx): fixed red blood cells or beads are excluded from a halo around living cells whose thickness reports the HA coat, which collapses after hyaluronidase treatment.
note: No evidence window describes the particle exclusion assay: nothing mentions fixed red blood cells or beads being excluded from a halo around living cells, or the coat collapsing after hyaluronidase; the windows discuss glycocalyx thickness/PBR measurements and hyaluronidase effects on glycocalyx permeation only.

final_answer: Fermentation produces a statistical distribution of chain lengths set by enzyme processivity and broth conditions; stepwise enzymatic synthesis with pmHAS and controlled UDP-sugar feeding builds defined-length, near-monodisperse chains.
note: Evidence supports the chemoenzymatic half only in part (PMC11673988: PmHAS gives 'very defined HA polymers' via stepwise extension yielding 'homogeneous oligosaccharides'), but no window addresses fermentation at all - nothing on fermentation producing a statistical chain-length distribution set by processivity or broth conditions - so the contrast the question asks about is not settled.

final_answer: pmHAS, the hyaluronan synthase from Pasteurella multocida, a bifunctional glycosyltransferase usable in vitro for one-pot synthesis of size-controlled HA oligosaccharides.
note: Evidence PMC6888640 describes one-pot HA synthesis using 'hyaluronan synthase from Pasteurella multocida (PmHAS)' with size adjusted via the UDP-sugar ratio; PMC11673988 states Class II PmHAS from Pasteurella multocida Type A is useful for very defined HA polymers in vitro.
